    Class
    Description
    EgradxAuthorityDto
     
    EgradxAuthResult
    Result of a successful login: a bearer access token, an opaque refresh token, the organization the access token is scoped to, the role held there, and the flat set of granular authority names that role resolves to at the moment of login only — a snapshot for immediate UI use, not authoritative for anything after that moment.
    EgradxCreateAuthorityRequest
     
    EgradxCreateOrganizationRequest
    Creating an organization always creates its first administrator too — an organization with no one able to sign into it is not a useful thing to have made.
    EgradxCreateOrganizationUserRequest
    Creating a user directly into an organization with a role — the admin action, as opposed to EgradxSignupRequest's self-service registration which lands a user in no organization at all.
    EgradxCreateRoleRequest
    authorityNames must already exist (create them first via POST /egradx/auth/authorities) — this does not implicitly create new authorities, so a typo here fails loudly with a 404 instead of quietly granting nothing.
    EgradxLoginRequest
    Login input for EgradxAuthService.login(...).

    EgradxReplaceRolePermissionsRequest
    Full replace, matching what a "tick the boxes and save" permission matrix actually does — an empty set strips the role back to granting nothing.

    A role and the permissions it grants, resolved.
    EgradxSignupRequest

    EgradxUpdateOrganizationRequest
    An organization's editable state as one thing, because that is how an edit form submits it — rather than making a caller work out that a rename is a PATCH but a suspension is a different verb on a different path.
    EgradxUpdateOrganizationUserRequest
    Partial update of a user within an organization — every field is optional, and null leaves that attribute untouched.
